newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-SWEDISH QUARTET REPRESENT CHANGING OF GUARD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SWEDISH QUARTET REPRESENT CHANGING OF GUARD.

text.p: A quartet seeking their country's sixth Davis Cup title this weekend against France represent the changing face of Swedish tennis.
Stefan Edberg, 30, the supreme stylist of his generation, will grace the Cup for the last time while the current Swedish number one Thomas Enqvist plays in his first final.
Doubles specialists Nicklas Kulti and Jonas Bjorkman make up the rest of the side although Bjorkman is a doubtful starter because of a knee injury.
"The Davis Cup is very important for Sweden," said Jan Bergstrom, a spokesman for the Swedish Tennis Federation.
"Players are so proud to play for Sweden in the Davis Cup. They receive very little money but it is the prestige that is important."
Win or lose, Edberg will be in the spotlight in his last tournament before retiring from the international circuit after 14 years.
Winning six grand slam titles during a distinguished career that included two years as the world number one, Edberg has become one of Sweden's sporting greats.
After an indifferent start to the season, the 22-year-old Enqvist is ending the year on a spectacular note, notching up victories in Paris and Stockholm in recent weeks.
The foursome will take on France's Guy Forget, Guillaume Raoux, Cedric Pioline, and French number one Arnaud Boetsch who toppled Enqvist in the semifinals of the Lyon grand prix last month.
Sweden's non-playing team captain Carl-Axel Hageskog announced last month that the final would be played on a fast, hard-court surface, generally preferred by Swedes.
Harsh winters in Sweden rule out outdoor training for six months of the year so most players are used to playing indoors and on hard surfaces.
The final will be played in a former shipyard workshop, now converted into a sports and exhibition complex, in Malmo, southern Sweden from November 29 to December 1.
The tournament is a suitable swansong for Edberg who first joined the Davis Cup squad in 1983 and has been in the winning team four times.
"He is very keen to play for one last time in the Davis Cup," Bergstrom said. "It is a good ending for him."
